> Still cPitchPal is a pocket-sized Tamagotchi-style virtual pet for soccer fans. It's a little striker you feed, train, and keep rested. It runs on an ESP32-C3 with a 1.3" OLED, three buttons, and a buzzer, and lives in a custom 3D-printed shell I'm designing myself. Its stats (hunger, energy, happiness, fitness) change over time and are saved to flash, so it keeps living when switched off. Mini-games include penalty kicks and juggling, and it evolves based on how well I look after it. Stretch goal: Wi-Fi time sync, plus a status page hosted on my homelab.oming up with the ideas

## Design

### 2026-10-03 — I defined the concept and rules for PitchPal, my soccer-themed Tamagotchi-style desk pet, and made the main design decisions for how it will work.

**2h**

I defined the concept and rules for PitchPal, my soccer-themed Tamagotchi-style desk pet, and made the main design decisions for how it will work.

What I decided

Concept: A young striker that starts as a ball with eyes and grows into a club legend, shown on a 128x64 OLED.
Stats (0-100): Hunger, energy, happiness, and fitness, each dropping over time at its own rate and each fixed by a different action (feed, sleep, play, train).
Controls: Three buttons (left, select, right), with a 2-second select hold to go back home.
Evolution: Ball Pup, then Rookie, then Starter, then Captain (good care) or Benchwarmer (poor care), based on a hidden care score.
Mini-games: Penalty kick (aim, then shoot against a randomly diving keeper) and juggling (timing-based combo).
Time handling: A hybrid design. The pet keeps time with its own timer while on, saves stats and a timestamp to flash, and on startup uses Wi-Fi (NTP) to catch up on time spent switched off. Offline decay is capped at about 8-12 hours and stats stop at a floor, and without Wi-Fi it simply resumes where it left off.
Debug mode: A fast-forward mode so I can test the evolution stages without waiting days.

Why these choices
I wanted a pet that is fair to the player: no punishing weekends away, and it still works without Wi-Fi. Building a pause-only version first and layering Wi-Fi catch-up on top means I always have a working pet.

Next
Sketching every screen (home, menu, status, and the mini-games) on paper.
